question: What will the first reported revenues after September 2026 be for the following companies? (Nvidia)

calls.reasoning: Nvidia guided Q3 FY27 at $108.0B ±2% (Aug 2026, ex-China DC compute). Over the last 8 quarters actual revenue beat the guide midpoint by 2.5-7.9% (mean ~5%, SD ~1.5%); Q2 FY27 beat by ~5.7% ($96.2B vs ~$91B). Applying the beat distribution gives a median of ~$113.3B. Upside tail >$116B (beat >7.4%) via a faster Rubin ramp or China sales resuming, ~9%. Downside below the low end of guidance is historically absent. Manifold (thin: 18 trades, 4 holders, same contract) puts 8% on <110, 40% on 110-112, 26% on 112-114, 17% on 114-116 and 10% on >=116, slightly lower than my beat-based median; I give it small weight.
calls.dossier:
- Nvidia Q2 FY27 (reported late Aug 2026): revenue $96.2B, data center ~$89B (+117% y/y) (dataporium.tech; stocktitan).
- Q3 FY27 guidance: $108.0B ±2% (range $105.8-110.2B), GAAP GM 74.0% ±50bp, no China DC compute revenue assumed; Vera Rubin in full production (dataporium.tech, Aug 2026).
- Consensus at the time of guidance was ~$103.5-104.2B (techflowpost). Later consensus figures by source: MarketBeat $108.8B, ChartMill $111.3B, RexShares $103.8B (varying dates).
- MarketBeat lists the report date as Nov 18, 2026 after close; the question text says no earlier than Nov 25. Either date is inside the window.
- Beat history (actual vs guide midpoint): Q3FY25 32.5->35.1 (+7.9%); Q4FY25 37.5->39.3 (+4.9%); Q1FY26 43->44.06 (+2.5%, H20 export hit); Q2FY26 45->46.74 (+3.9%); Q3FY26 54->57.0 (+5.6%); Q4FY26 65->68.1 (+4.8%); Q1FY27 ~78->81.6 (+4.6%); Q2FY27 ~91->96.2 (+5.7%). Q1/Q2 FY27 guide midpoints are inferred, not confirmed. Fool cites 12 straight quarters above the high end of guidance, averaging 3.1% above the high end over the last 4.
- Sequential growth guided at ~12% vs 18% actual in Q2.
- Upside mechanisms: faster Rubin ramp, China H20/other sales resuming (not in guide). Downside: supply/CoWoS constraints, export rules, Rubin transition hiccups.
- Human market: thin Manifold market exists (same contract).
- Resolves off the initially reported Q3 FY27 total revenue in the 8-K/press release, not later revisions and not segment figures.
- Event window: first quarterly release after Sep 30, 2026 -> before Jan 1, 2027. As of Oct 22, 2026 the release has not happened; it is expected mid/late November.
- Not found: any mid-quarter guidance update or pre-announcement.

calls.reasoning: Nvidia guided Q3 FY27 revenue to $108.0B +/-2%, excluding China data-center compute. Over the last 8 quarters it beat the guide midpoint by 2.5-7.9% (about 5% on average; the last 4 were 4.6-5.7%), which centres the outcome near $113.0-113.4B. Revenue above $116B needs a beat over 7.4%, seen once in 8 quarters; China sales resuming or a faster Rubin ramp could cause it, so I put ~10% there. Below $105B means missing the guidance floor, which hasn't happened in at least 12 quarters (~1%). The percentiles are conditional on landing inside $105-116B, which pulls the median slightly below the unconditional ~$113.3B. Market check: the runs found only a thin Manifold market with the same contract (4 holders) that clusters at $110-114B, slightly lower; no Polymarket, Kalshi or bookmaker market found.
calls.reconciliation: All three runs agree on the guide ($108.0B +/-2%, ex-China), the beat history (2.5-7.9%, about 5% typical), and that the release falls inside the window. Remaining factual gaps: the report date (Nov 17/18/25, all inside the window, so it doesn't matter) and some older guide midpoints that are partly from memory, which only Q2 FY27 confirms; I couldn't verify either without web access. Neither changes the centre. The only real disagreement is judgment on tail mass (8-10% above $116B, 0-1% below $105B). I took 10%/1% because China upside is excluded from the guide and dollar beats are growing. Unlike the runs, I stated the percentiles explicitly conditional on landing in-range, so the median is $113.0B rather than ~$113.2B. I carried forward the runs' reference class and the ~$4.1B dispersion.
